cohort: The study included 260 preterm infants of at least 35 weeks gestational age admitted on continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), excluding those requiring less than 24 hours of CPAP or diagnosed with meconium aspiration syndrome.
finding: Implementing the respiratory care protocol increased surfactant use and was associated with improved oxygenation and respiratory severity scores, but did not significantly improve major clinical outcomes such as mechanical ventilation, pneumothorax, or length of hospital stay.
followup_time: Up to 48 hours for specific respiratory parameters, and length of hospital stay
